# Refusals

<!-- Generated by scripts/refusals.py from the catalog; do not edit it by hand. -->

What a refusal of `invalid`, `constraint`, `precondition`, `declined` or
`unanswered` says, as data: a case's `code`, its parameters, and the sentence they
make, which is the case's only sentence. A case is said at places (`at`,
outermost first), each a case of `Place`; the sentence is the places,
joined by `, `, then `: ` and the case's. On the wire a case and a place
are objects: `code`, the parameters by the names below, and `message`.
A host renders a code it knows in its users' language, and one it does
not know by its message. The rules a code keeps are in
`docs/decisions/015-errors-are-a-closed-set-writes-answer-an-outcome.md`.

| `migration_takes_target` | `unnamed` (bool), `relation` (RelationName), `type` (TypeName) | [{?unnamed}a declaration\|it] refers to `{type}`, the link type of the relation `{relation}`, which the migration removes; retarget or remove it first | A migration that removes a relation whose link type another relation or a reference field refers to. |
| `migration_takes_read` | `unnamed` (bool), `field` (FieldName), `type` (TypeName), `renamed` (FieldName, optional) | [{?unnamed}a declaration\|it] reads `{field}` of `{type}`, which the migration [renames to `{renamed}`\|drops] | A migration that takes away a field a declaration reads. |
| `migration_to_view` | `type` (TypeName) | the migration would turn the stored type `{type}` into a view; declare the view under another name, and the type keeps its name and its records | A migration that would make a stored type a view. |
| `migration_view_to_stored` | `type` (TypeName) | `{type}` is a view, and it becomes a stored type by being declared as one, never by a migration | A migration that would make a view a stored type. |
| `narrowing_breaks_links` | `relation` (RelationName), `cardinality` (Cardinality), `count` (usize) | narrowing `{relation}` to {cardinality} would break the links of {count} record(s) that hold more than one; unlink them first | A narrowing of a cardinality that existing links break. |
| `no_longer_declarable` | `type` (TypeName) | a declaration over `{type}` could no longer be declared | A declaration over a migrated type that could not be declared again. |
| `reads_taken_away` | — | a declaration reads a field the migration takes away | A field taken away that a declaration the author does not know reads. |
| `rekey_ring` | `type` (TypeName), `ring` (Names) | re-keying `{type}` would move keys that are made of keys it moves, in {ring}; no order makes them, so that is not supported | Re-keying that moves keys made of each other. |
| `rekey_system` | `type` (TypeName), `system` (TypeName) | re-keying `{type}` would re-key the system type `{system}`, which is keyed by it; that is not supported | Re-keying that would re-key a system type. |
| `rekey_view` | `type` (TypeName), `view` (TypeName) | re-keying `{type}` would re-key the view `{view}`, which is keyed by it; a view's rows are computed and cannot be moved, so that is not supported | Re-keying that would re-key a view. |
| `relation_rename_changes` | — | a rename keeps the relation's carrier, target, cardinality, link fields and authority; change them in a migration of their own | A relation rename that changes more than the name. |
| `relation_rename_names_none` | — | the first names a relation the type has, the second one the new shape has | A relation rename naming relations that are not there. |
| `relation_rename_not_once` | — | a relation is renamed once, to a name no relation of the type bears, and leaves its old name free | A relation renamed twice, or to a name in use. |
| `rename_collides` | `to` (FieldName) | rename to `{to}`: that field already exists and keeps its values | A field renamed to one that keeps its own values. |
| `rename_from_unknown` | `from` (FieldName) | rename from `{from}`: no such field before the migration | A field renamed from one the type does not have. |
| `rename_name_held` | — | the lake keeps the links of an earlier relation of that name; take another name | A relation rename to a name whose links the lake keeps. |
| `rename_referred_links` | `type` (TypeName, optional), `links` (TypeName) | [`{type}`\|a declaration] refers to its link type `{links}`, whose records would move; retarget it first | A relation rename whose link type another declaration refers to. |
| `rename_repeated` | `field` (FieldName) | the field `{field}` is renamed more than once | A field renamed from or to twice. |
| `fill_unknown` | `field` (FieldName) | the migration fills `{field}`, which the new declaration does not declare | A field a migration fills that its new declaration does not declare. |
| `fill_no_initial` | `field` (FieldName) | the migration fills `{field}`, which declares no `initial` to fill it with | A field a migration fills that declares no initial value. |
| `fill_repeated` | `field` (FieldName) | the migration fills `{field}` more than once | A field a migration fills more than once. |
| `fill_renamed` | `field` (FieldName), `to` (FieldName) | the migration renames `{field}` to `{to}`; fill it as `{to}` | A field a migration fills by the name a rename takes away. |
| `rename_to_unknown` | `to` (FieldName) | rename to `{to}`: no such field after the migration | A field renamed to one the new declaration does not have. |
| `rename_while_rekeying` | — | the same migration re-keys records; rename in one migration and re-key in another | A relation rename in a migration that re-keys. |
| `remove_while_rekeying` | — | the same migration re-keys records; remove the relation in one migration and re-key in another | A relation carried by link records removed by a migration that re-keys records. |
| `reshapes` | `type` (TypeName), `reasons` (list of Revision) | `{type}` would reshape stored records ({reasons}); that is a migration | A declaration that reshapes stored records. |
| `reshapes_links` | `type` (TypeName), `links` (TypeName), `reasons` (list of Revision) | `{type}` would reshape the links `{links}` holds ({reasons}); that is a migration | A declaration that reshapes stored links. |
| `value_rename_new_refused` | — | the new value is one the new declaration accepts | A rename's new value the new declaration does not accept. |
| `value_rename_not_text` | `value_type` (ValueTypeName) | value type `{value_type}` is not text: only a text value type renames its values | A value rename of a value type that is not text. |

| `value_rename_twice` | — | a value is renamed once | A value renamed twice. |

| `value_type_not_tightened` | `value_type` (ValueTypeName), `misfits` (u64), `first` (list of RecordName) | value type `{value_type}` is not tightened: {misfits} stored value(s) or a field's declared `initial` would not fit it; change them first.[ First: {first}] | A value type tightened while stored values would not fit it. |
| `value_type_reshapes` | `value_type` (ValueTypeName) | value type `{value_type}` would change its `kind` or `scale`, which rewrites stored values; that is not a value-type migration: migrate the fields that use it | A value type declared with another kind or scale. |

| `value_type_tightens` | `value_type` (ValueTypeName) | value type `{value_type}` would accept less than it does: stored values may stop fitting it; tighten it through `migrate`, whose preflight counts them, or propose it as a value type's migration | A value type declared to accept less. |

| `geo_unknown_type` | `name` (String) | not a GeoJSON geometry: "{name}" is not a geometry type | A geometry of a type GeoJSON does not have. |

| `not_base64` | — | not standard base64 with padding | Bytes that are not base64. |

## `Operand`

A value an expression computed, as a case names it.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `null` | — | null | Null. |
| `boolean` | `value` (bool) | the boolean [{?value}true\|false] | A boolean. |
| `number` | `value` (String) | the number `{value}` | A number. |
| `text` | `value` (String) | the text '{value}' | Text. |
| `instant` | `value` (Timestamp) | the instant `{value}` | An instant. |
| `duration` | `micros` (i64) | a duration of {micros} microseconds | A duration. |
| `json` | — | a JSON value | A JSON array or object. |

|---|---|---|---|

| `category_brace` | `p` (char) | `\\{p}` must be followed by a category in braces | A category escape with no category in braces. |
| `category_range` | — | a range cannot end in a category | A class's range that ends in a category. |
| `class_unclosed` | — | a character class is not closed | A class not closed. |
| `dash_in_class` | — | `-` inside a class must be first, last or escaped | A `-` inside a class, not first or last. |
| `ends_in_backslash` | — | the pattern ends with `\\` | A pattern ending in `\`. |
| `group_unclosed` | — | a group is not closed with `)` | A group not closed. |
| `must_escape` | `c` (char) | `{c}` must be escaped | A character that must be escaped. |
| `must_escape_in_class` | `c` (char) | `{c}` must be escaped inside a class | A bracket inside a class. |
| `not_category` | `name` (String) | `{name}` is not a Unicode general category | A category the grammar does not know. |
| `not_repetition` | `body` (String) | `{body}` between braces is not a repetition | Braces that hold no repetition. |
| `quantifier_twice` | — | a quantifier cannot follow a quantifier | A quantifier after a quantifier. |
| `range_backwards` | `lo` (char), `hi` (char) | the range `{lo}-{hi}` runs backwards | A class's range that runs backwards. |
| `repeats_backwards` | `body` (String) | `{body}` between braces repeats at least more than at most | A repetition whose least is more than its most. |
| `unmatched` | `c` (char) | unexpected `{c}` (an unmatched `)`?) | A character left after the whole pattern. |

## `Beyond`

What a constraint reads that can change without a write of its record (lakelands#1119).

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | — | a path across a reference or a link | A path across a reference or a link. |
| `in_set` | — | `in_set` | An object set. |
| `setting` | — | `setting` | A setting. |
| `clock` | — | the clock | The clock. |
| `exists` | — | `exists` | A relation's links. |
| `computed_outside` | `field` (FieldName) | `{field}`, computed outside the lake | A field computed outside the lake. |
| `computed_at_read` | `field` (FieldName) | `{field}`, computed at the read | A field computed at the read. |

## `Revision`

One difference between two declarations of a type; a field's names the relation whose links carry it.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field_added` | `field` (FieldName), `relation` (RelationName, optional), `required` (bool) | [{?required}required\|optional] field `{field}`[ of relation `{relation}`] added | A field added; it reshapes when required. |
| `field_removed` | `field` (FieldName), `relation` (RelationName, optional) | field `{field}`[ of relation `{relation}`] removed | A field removed; it reshapes. |
| `field_retyped` | `field` (FieldName), `relation` (RelationName, optional), `from` (FieldType), `to` (FieldType) | field `{field}`[ of relation `{relation}`] changes type from {from} to {to} | A field's type changed; it reshapes. |
| `field_required` | `field` (FieldName), `relation` (RelationName, optional) | field `{field}`[ of relation `{relation}`] becomes required | An optional field made required; it reshapes. |
| `field_optional` | `field` (FieldName), `relation` (RelationName, optional) | field `{field}`[ of relation `{relation}`] becomes optional | A required field made optional. |
| `key_changed` | `from` (Names), `to` (Names) | the key changes from {from} to {to} | The key's fields or their order changed; it reshapes. |
| `relation_added` | `relation` (RelationName) | relation `{relation}` added | A relation added. |
| `relation_removed` | `relation` (RelationName) | relation `{relation}` removed | A relation removed; it reshapes. |
| `relation_retargeted` | `relation` (RelationName), `from` (TypeName), `to` (TypeName) | relation `{relation}` points at `{to}` instead of `{from}` | A relation that points at another type; it reshapes. |
| `cardinality_changed` | `relation` (RelationName), `from` (Cardinality), `to` (Cardinality) | relation `{relation}` changes cardinality from {from} to {to} | A relation's cardinality changed; it reshapes unless it widens. |
| `view_changed` | — | the view changes | A view's source, filter, grouping or measures changed. |
| `became_view` | — | a stored type becomes a view | A stored type made a view; it reshapes. |
| `stopped_being_view` | — | a view becomes a stored type | A view made a stored type. |

## `Seam`

A seam the call needs and the host has not bound.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `executor` | `name` (String) | the verb executor `{name}` | A verb's executor, by the name the verb declares. |
| `embedding` | `model` (String), `dimensions` (u32), `type` (TypeName), `field` (String), `bound` (Bound, optional) | the embedding model `{model}` with {dimensions} dimensions, for `{type}.{field}` [(the bound one is {bound})\|(none is bound)] | An embedding backend for a field's model: none is bound, or one of another model or length. |
| `function_backing` | `kind` (String) | the `{kind}` function backing (the host bound none of that kind) | A function backing of a kind. |
| `key_store` | — | a key store, which seals a source's values of an erasable field (the host bound none) | A key store, which seals a source's values of an erasable field. |
| `key_versions` | — | a key store that destroys a version of a source's key with every older one (the bound one destroys only a whole source's) | A key store that destroys a version of a source's key with those before it. |
| `vector_index` | — | a vector index (this engine keeps none) | A vector index, which this engine keeps none of. |
| `engine` | `name` (String) | the engine `{name}` (no opener for it was passed in) | An engine, whose opener was not passed in. |
| `operation` | `op` (String) | the host operation `{op}`, which this door does not offer | An operation of the host's that this door does not offer. |

## `Remote`

A remote end a call reaches: an embedding backend, a function's backing, a REST door.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embedding` | `model` (String) | the embedding backend `{model}` | The embedding backend of a model. |
| `executor` | `name` (String) | the verb executor `{name}` | A verb's executor. |
| `function` | `function` (String) | function `{function}` | A function's backing. |
| `door` | `lake` (String) | the REST door of lake `{lake}` | A lake's REST door. |

## `Flaw`

What is wrong with stored or exported events, a checkpoint, or the files that hold them.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `not_json` | `detail` (Detail) | a line is not JSON: {detail} | A line is not JSON. |
| `not_an_event` | `detail` (Detail) | a line is not an event: {detail} | A line is not an event. |
| `not_canonical` | — | the bytes are not canonical | The bytes are not canonical. |
| `not_one_form` | — | a member is not in its one written form | A member is not in its one written form. |
| `format_other` | `v` (u64), `reads` (u64) | written in log format {v}, which this release does not read; it writes format {reads} | It is written in a log format this release does not read. |
| `created_in_another` | `format` (u64), `reads` (u64) | its `lake_created` says log format {format}, another than its own line's or one this release does not read; it writes format {reads} | Its `lake_created` says another log format than its own line, or one the release does not read. |
| `fence_below` | `fence` (u64), `floor` (u64) | it carries fence {fence}, below the fence {floor} of the event before it: fences never fall | Its fence is below the fence of the event before it. |
| `format_step` | `v` (u64), `before` (u64) | written in log format {v} after an event in format {before}: a lake's format rises only at a new writer's `lease_taken`, whose next event is the `lake_upgraded` from the one to the other | Its log format differs from the event's before it where no new writer upgraded the lake. |
| `cause_in_context` | — | `context` carries `cause`, which the envelope carries | `context` carries `cause`, which the envelope carries. |
| `initial_origin` | — | the envelope carries the origin `initial`, a field's alone | The envelope carries the origin `initial`, a field's alone. |
| `sealed_on` | `kind` (String) | a `{kind}` event carries `sealed`, which only a `record_ingested` or an `output_recorded` carries | An event other than `record_ingested` and `output_recorded` carries `sealed`. |
| `sealed_before` | `v` (u32) | an event of format {v} carries `sealed`, which format 16 added | An event of a format before 16 carries `sealed`. |
| `forgotten_before` | `v` (u32) | an event of format {v} is a `source_forgotten`, which format 16 added | A `source_forgotten` in a format before the one that added it. |
| `delivery_on` | `kind` (String), `v` (u32) | a `{kind}` event of format {v} carries `delivery`, which only a `record_ingested` of format 17 on carries | An event other than a `record_ingested` of format 17 on carries `delivery`. |
| `upstream_on` | `kind` (String) | a `{kind}` event carries `upstream`, which only a `record_ingested` event carries | An event other than `record_ingested` carries `upstream`. |
| `hash_mismatch` | — | the hash does not match the event | The hash does not match the event. |
| `disagrees` | — | the engine's record of the event disagrees with its bytes | The engine's record of the event disagrees with its bytes. |
| `position` | `expected` (Position), `found` (Position, optional) | [position {found} stands where \|expected ]position {expected}[{?found} belongs] | Another position stands where one belongs, or none does. |
| `prev_hash` | — | it does not name the hash of the event before it | It does not name the hash of the event before it. |
| `known_at_back` | `known_at` (Timestamp), `before` (Timestamp) | its known_at {known_at} is before the {before} of the event before it | Its `known_at` is before that of the event before it. |
| `integer_too_large` | `n` (Number) | the integer {n} in it is beyond ±(2^53 − 1), which not every reader reads exactly | It holds a number written as an integer beyond ±(2^53 − 1). |
| `no_checkpoint` | — | a segment begins there, and its first event is no checkpoint | A segment begins there, and its first event is no checkpoint. |
| `ends_before` | `position` (Position) | it ends before position {position} | It ends before a position it should hold. |
| `ends_inside_set` | — | it ends inside a set of declarations: the set's last declaration is missing | It ends inside a set of declarations. |
| `no_event` | `position` (Position) | it holds no event at position {position} | It holds no event at the position. |
| `moves_unheld` | `type` (TypeName), `key` (RecordKey) | a migration moves `{type}` `{key}`, which the lake does not hold | A migration moves a key the lake does not hold. |
| `renames_other_types` | `value_type` (String) | it renames values of `{value_type}` in other types than those that use it | A value type's renames reach other types than those that use it. |
| `output_once` | — | an `output_recorded` event carries both `output` and `output_at`, or neither | An `output_recorded` event carries both `output` and `output_at`, or neither. |
| `not_latest_output` | `at` (Position) | it names the output at position {at}, which is not its call's latest output | It names an output that is not its call's latest. |
| `own_seam` | `seam` (String) | it records under `{seam}`: a seam that begins `sys:` is the store's own | It records under a seam that is the store's own. |
| `own_type` | `type` (TypeName) | it declares or writes the type `{type}`: a name that begins `sys:` is the store's own, for what it keeps of a view | It declares or writes a type whose name is the store's own. |
| `view_record` | `type` (TypeName) | it writes a record of `{type}`, a view, whose records are computed | It writes a record of a view. |
| `checkpoint_follows` | `through` (Position) | the checkpoint says it follows position {through} | A checkpoint does not follow the position before it. |
| `checkpoint_hash` | — | the checkpoint's hash is not the hash of the event before it | A checkpoint's hash is not that of the event before it. |
| `checkpoint_range` | `first` (Position), `last` (Position), `next` (u64) | the checkpoint's segment list has the range {first}..={last} where one starting at {next} belongs | A checkpoint's segment list has a range out of place. |
| `checkpoint_end` | `through` (Position) | the checkpoint's segment list does not end at position {through} | A checkpoint's segment list does not end where it does. |
| `segment_differs` | `first` (Position), `at` (Position) | the segment from position {first} differs from what the checkpoint at {at} recorded | A segment differs from what a checkpoint recorded. |
| `segment_missing` | `first` (Position), `at` (Position) | the segment from position {first} is missing; the checkpoint at {at} records it | A segment a checkpoint records is missing. |
| `cannot_convert` | `type` (TypeName), `key` (RecordKey) | a migration cannot convert `{type}` `{key}` | A migration cannot convert a record. |
| `changed_unwritten` | `type` (TypeName), `key` (RecordKey) | it changes `{type}` `{key}` before any event wrote it | The log changes a record before any event wrote it. |
| `out_of_key_order` | `type` (TypeName), `key` (RecordKey), `before` (RecordKey) | the engine handed `{type}` out of key order, `{key}` after `{before}` | The engine handed records out of key order. |
| `proposal_without_write` | `proposal` (ProposalId) | it holds proposal `{proposal}` without its write | A stored proposal holds no write. |
| `unreadable` | `what` (String), `detail` (Detail) | it holds {what} it cannot read: {detail} | The projection holds something it cannot read, named as its table names it. |
| `no_schema_hash` | `type` (TypeName) | the system type `{type}` has no schema hash | A system type has no schema hash. |
| `cannot_order` | `type` (TypeName), `cause` (Error) | the fold cannot order the computed fields of `{type}`: {cause} | The fold cannot order a type's computed fields. |
| `cannot_derive` | `type` (TypeName), `cause` (Error) | the fold cannot compute the derived fields of `{type}`: {cause} | The fold cannot compute a type's derived fields. |
| `unknown_line` | — | it holds a line it does not know | A line of a kind it does not know. |
| `commit_without_event` | — | its last commit line follows no event of its segment | Its last commit line follows no event of its segment. |
| `checkpoint_not_first` | — | a checkpoint is not the first event of a later file | A checkpoint is not the first event of a later file. |
| `checkpoint_prev` | — | the checkpoint does not name the position and hash before it | A checkpoint does not name the position and hash before it. |
| `checkpoint_files` | — | the checkpoint does not list the files before it | A checkpoint does not list the files before it. |
| `later_without_checkpoint` | — | a later file does not start with a checkpoint | A later file does not start with a checkpoint. |
| `next_file` | `name` (String), `first` (u64) | the next file is {name}, starting at {first} | Another file follows than the one that belongs. |
| `file_name` | `name` (String) | the file {name} is not named by a first position in 20 digits | A file is not named by a first position in 20 digits. |
| `no_line_feed` | `name` (String) | the file {name} does not end in a line feed | A file does not end in a line feed. |
| `no_event_in` | `name` (String) | the file {name} holds no event | A file holds no event. |
| `no_segment_file` | — | there is no segment file under log/ | There is no segment file. |
| `index_missing` | `name` (String) | the segment {name} has no index file | A segment has no index file beside it. |
| `fence_mismatch` | `carried` (u64), `lease` (u64) | an event carries fence {carried}, and its writer's lease had fence {lease} | An event carries another fence than its writer's lease had. |

| `truncated` | — | it ends before its committed events do | A file ends before its committed events do. |

## `Situation`

Why the lake cannot answer now. Retrying may help; the sentence says what the operator can do.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lease_held` | `holder` (String), `fence` (u64) | the lake's writer lease is held by `{holder}` (fence {fence}); it must be released before another writer can take it | Another writer holds the lake's writer lease. |
| `lease_locked` | `holder` (String, optional), `fence` (u64) | the lake's writer lease cannot be taken: its lock is held, and the lease row [names `{holder}` ](fence {fence})[{?holder}\| names no holder]. Either that writer holds it, or a writer's session is still ending, or another schema's name hashes to the same lock; retry once the writer is gone, or give this lake another schema | The lease's lock is held: by the writer its row names, by a session still ending, or by another schema whose name shares the lock. |
| `lease_stale` | `fence` (u64), `holder` (String, optional), `current` (u64, optional), `undone` (Act, optional) | the lease with fence {fence} is stale: [`{holder}` holds the lake's writer lease[ with fence {current}]\|[the lease row records fence {current} and no holder\|no one holds the lake's writer lease]][; {undone}] | The caller's lease is stale: another holds the lake's lease now, or no one does. |
| `lease_not_held` | `fence` (u64, optional), `undone` (Act, optional) | the lease[ with fence {fence}] is not held by this handle[; {undone}] | The caller's lease is not held by this handle. |
| `read_only` | `lake` (String, optional), `leased_elsewhere` (bool) | [lake `{lake}`\|this lake] is open read-only here[{?leased_elsewhere}; another process holds its writer lease\|[{?lake}; open it for writing to take the lease]] | The lake is open read-only here; whether another process holds its writer lease. |
| `no_lake` | `lake` (String), `schema` (String, optional) | there is no lake `{lake}` [in the schema `{schema}`\|where its location says]; open it with `create` to make it | There is no lake where the location says, in the schema looked in where the engine keeps one per lake. |
| `not_served` | `lake` (String) | this server serves no lake `{lake}` | This server serves no lake of the name. |
| `unmade` | `part` (Part) | this engine did not create what is there: {part} is missing | A part every lake of this engine has is missing: something else made what is there. |
| `no_projection` | `lake` (String) | lake `{lake}` has no projection yet; open it for writing first | The lake has no projection yet. |
| `projection_layout` | `lake` (String), `found` (u64, optional), `wanted` (u64) | lake `{lake}`'s projection [has layout {found}\|has no layout number], and this build reads layout {wanted}; nothing was read from it: rebuild it from the log with `lakelands rebuild` | The lake's projection was laid out by another build: nothing reads it, and a rebuild makes it anew from the log. |
| `log_format` | `lake` (String), `found` (u64), `reads` (u64), `oldest` (u64, optional) | lake `{lake}` is written in log format {found}, and this release reads log format[s {oldest} to] {reads} and writes {reads}; nothing was read from it and nothing appended | The lake's log is written in the format of another release: nothing reads it and nothing is appended. |
| `log_upgrade_owed` | `lake` (String), `found` (u64), `reads` (u64) | lake `{lake}` is written in log format {found}, and this release writes format {reads}: a writer's open upgrades it, so open it once for writing or run `lakelands upgrade {lake}`, and it is read; nothing was read from it | The lake's log is written in an older format this release reads, and only a writer's open upgrades it. |
| `busy` | `lake` (String) | lake `{lake}` could not be compacted: a reader holds a snapshot of its projection; nothing a read answers has changed, so compact again when the reader is done | The lake could not be compacted while a reader holds a snapshot. |
| `behind` | `cause` (Error, optional) | the lake's projection is behind its log and could not catch up; nothing was appended[ ({cause})] | The projection is behind the log and could not catch up; nothing was appended. |
| `key_missing` | `source` (SourceId), `key` (KeyId) | the key store does not give the key `{key}` of the source `{source}`, and no act forgot that source; a lost key is never read as an erasure | A key of a source that the key store does not give, with no act that forgot the source. |
| `unsealable` | `position` (Position) | a sealed value of the event at position {position} does not open under the key it names: the key store gives another key under that id, or the event was changed | A sealed value that does not open under the key its event names. |
| `decided_behind` | — | this write was decided while the lake's projection was behind its log; nothing was appended | The write was decided while the projection was behind the log; nothing was appended. |
| `not_folded` | `from` (Position), `cause` (Error) | what was appended is in the log from position {from} and is not folded yet; the next write folds it, and a write is sent again only under its idempotency key ({cause}) | What was appended from a position is in the log and not folded yet. |
| `moved` | — | the lake's names moved while this write waited; send it again | The lake's names moved while the write waited; send it again. |
| `types_moved` | — | the lake's types moved while this write waited; send it again | The types a write reads, or what its principal is shown of them, moved while the write waited; send it again. |
| `executor` | `retry` (Retry), `cause` (Error) | the verb's executor was not handed this call ({cause}); {retry} | A call of a verb that reaches outside the lake failed before its executor was handed it. |
| `answer_held` | `answered` (Value), `retry` (Resent, optional), `cause` (Error) | the verb's executor answered this call, and recording its answer, {answered}, failed: {cause}; the answer is held and recorded before the next write[; {retry}] | A call's executor answered, recording its answer failed, and the answer is held and recorded before the next write; what sending it again answers, unless it has no key. |
| `answer_lost` | `answered` (Value), `cause` (Error) | the verb's executor answered this call with {answered}, and recording its answer failed: {cause} | A call's executor answered, and recording its answer failed. |
| `stopped` | `detail` (Detail) | the store's work stopped unexpectedly: {detail} | The store's work stopped unexpectedly. |
| `damaged` | `part` (Part), `position` (Position, optional), `flaw` (Flaw) | {part} is damaged[ at position {position}]: {flaw} | Stored or exported events, or the files that hold them, are damaged, at a position if one. |
| `storage` | `doing` (Doing), `part` (Part), `detail` (Detail) | the storage failed while {doing} {part}: {detail} | The storage failed. |
| `append_failed` | `detail` (Detail), `left` (Left), `cut` (Error, optional) | appending to the log failed: {detail}[; {left}][ ({cut})] | An append to the log failed; what it left, and why the cut after it failed where it did. |
| `unsynced` | — | a sync of the log failed on this handle and writing it again failed too, so it writes nothing more: open the lake again, and its open checks what the last append left | A sync of the log failed on this handle, and writing and syncing its group again failed too: it appends, seals and takes the lease no more until the lake is opened again, whose open checks the group it left. |
| `seal_unsure` | `detail` (Detail) | syncing the log's directory failed: {detail}; the next segment is in the log's files and its name's sync failed: every handle reads it, and the outcome is not known | A seal's step was taken and syncing its directory failed: the next segment is in the log's files, and the outcome is not known. |
| `sealed_not_read` | `last` (Position), `cause` (Error) | the segment through position {last} is sealed and the next one is in the log's files, synced; this handle then failed to read on: {cause} | A segment was sealed through a position, and this handle then failed to read on. |
| `compact_failed` | `lake` (String), `detail` (Detail) | lake `{lake}` could not be compacted, and its projection is as it was: {detail} | A compaction failed, and the projection is as it was. |
| `import_not_folded` | `cause` (Error) | every event was imported, and folding the projection failed: {cause}; a writer's open folds it again | Every event was imported, and folding the projection failed. |
| `import_stopped` | `reached` (Position), `lake` (String), `cause` (Error) | the import stopped at position {reached}: {cause}; the lake `{lake}` holds the export's events before that position, a true prefix that is not the exported lake, and refuses another import; remove it and import again | An import stopped part way, at the position it reached. |
| `server_too_old` | `major` (u32), `minor` (u32) | the server is PostgreSQL {major}.{minor}; the engine needs PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and nothing was created | The PostgreSQL server is older than the engine needs. |
| `pooler` | — | the connection does not keep its session; a transaction-mode connection pooler seems to sit in front of the server. The writer lease is a session lock, which such a pooler loses or hands to another client, so the lake was not opened for writing. Connect directly or through a session-mode pooler. | A transaction-mode connection pooler seems to sit in front of the server. |
| `tls` | `problem` (Tls), `detail` (Detail, optional) | TLS cannot be set up: {problem}[: {detail}] | TLS cannot be set up for the lake's connection, with the library's words if it gave any. |
| `tool_names` | `problems` (list of NameProblem) | the lake's names cannot all become tools[: {problems}] | The lake's names cannot all become tools. |
| `remote` | `remote` (Remote), `exchange` (Exchange) | calling {remote}: {exchange} | An exchange with a remote end failed. |

## `NameSource`

A declaration a tool name comes from.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generic` | `tool` (String) | the generic tool `{tool}` | A generic tool, by its name. |
| `type` | `type` (TypeName) | type `{type}` | A type, whose doors are tools. |
| `verb` | `verb` (VerbName) | verb `{verb}` | A verb. |
| `link` | `relation` (RelationName), `type` (TypeName) | relation `{relation}` of type `{type}` | A relation of a type, whose link doors are tools. |

## `NameProblem`

Why a lake's declarations cannot all become tools. The store refuses a declaration that would introduce one of these, so [`tools`] never meets them in a lake the store wrote.

| code | parameters | sentence | about |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collision` | `name` (String), `from` (list of NameSource) | the tool name `{name}` would come from {from} | Two declarations produce the same tool name. |
| `too_long` | `name` (String) | the tool name `{name}` is longer than 64 characters | A tool name would be longer than [`MAX_TOOL_NAME`]. |
| `empty` | `from` (NameSource) | {from} gives an empty tool name | A declaration's name has nothing left once made a tool name. |

## Parameter types

A parameter of a set above is that set's case; a plain name is said by
its own sentence. The other types:

- **text** (`String`), a **name** (`TypeName`, `FieldName`, `RelationName`,
  `VerbName`, `ParamName`, `TriggerName`, `ConstraintName`,
  `ValueTypeName`, `LakeId`, `SourceId`, `KeyId`) or a **record key** (`RecordKey`): a string;
- a **number** (`u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `usize`, `i32`, `i64`, `Number`) or
  a **position** (`Position`): a JSON number;
- an **instant** (`Timestamp`): an RFC 3339 string in UTC; a
  **proposal's identifier** (`ProposalId`): a string;
- a **field's type** (`FieldType`): an object as a declaration writes
  it, `kind` and what the kind takes; a **bound backend** (`Bound`):
  `model` and `dimensions`;
- **`Names`**: a list of strings, said "`a`, `b`";
- **`Detail`**: an operating system's, a database's or a library's own
  words, scrubbed at their source; never a key, a value or a host path;
- **`Value`**: a JSON value the caller gave;
- **`Error`**: a nested error, as the error's own JSON;
- **`bool`**: a flag, said only by the segment it switches.

These types are said by a name of a closed list:

### `Authority`

Which authority writes a field. It decides which door may carry the field: a source feed through `ingest`, an author through `upsert` or a verb, the store itself through the fold. Grants then decide which principals of that authority may.

`authored`, `source`, `shared`, `derived`, `verb`

### `Cardinality`

How many records a relation links on each side.

`one_to_one`, `one_to_many`, `many_to_one`, `many_to_many`

### `Carrier`

How a relation's edges are carried.

`via`, `links`, `derived`

### `Kind`

What an expression certainly computes.

`boolean`, `number`, `text`, `instant`, `duration`

### `OrderBy`

What a sort key orders by: a field's value, or when it was learned or observed (`docs/decisions/010-provenance-per-field.md`), or, with no field, the position of the event that made each record's state (`docs/decisions/029-every-answer-has-one-order.md`).

`value`, `known_at`, `seen_at`, `latest`

### `StorageKind`

How an engine stores, compares and indexes a value. The set is closed: a kind exists only when an engine must treat it differently from every other kind (`docs/decisions/011-storage-kind-and-value-type.md`).

`text`, `number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date_time`, `bytes`, `json`, `reference`, `vector`, `geo`, `date`

### `Walk`

Which way a step walks a relation.

`out`, `in`, `both`
